scores.evidence: 'Morning' section opens 'If you only caught the last three laps on Sunday, you saw the right bit' — scene-setting, not a verdict
'Until next week' paragraph restates championship standings and previews Madrid — textbook summary/wrap-up violation
'Morning' section bridges with 'What you didn't see is why it was ever close' — a transitional sentence doing heading's work
'0.85 seconds a lap, taken off a hard tyre that was 40-odd laps old' — good, but 'Lap 40 to lap 48: the gap came down from 7.1s to 0.264s' clusters figures in same breath
'Call it an estimate, because it is' and 'I don't think so' and 'I'd rather say so than pretend otherwise' — hedges are explicit, owned, and never falsely neutral
'on equal-age rubber the faster car was going nowhere' — Russell is the constant teammate benchmark throughout; absolute comparisons only follow
FIA stewards penalty message quoted verbatim; track-limits deletion quoted with lap/time — both complicate or confirm the reading just given
'About that grid penalty' section recaps Antonelli's qualifying position, penalty cause, and restart order — partial narration of sequence rather than pure interpretation
'Monza doesn't let you pass a car of equal speed, and a car half a second quicker isn't enough either, apparently' — flat, dry, exactly right
'I think it matters more than anything else in this piece' — sentence about the piece itself, violating the rule directly
No introductions, no jargon glosses; 'VSC', 'green-flag stop', 'trace' used without explanation throughout
'Nobody thought much of it at the time. It turned out to be the whole afternoon.' — consistently tight; nearly every paragraph is 2-4 sentences making one point
'How much would that stop have cost at green-flag speed? About 31 seconds, going by the median pit-lane time in this race.' — long analytical setup, short punchy answer, sustained throughout
VSC mechanism gets the longest section; Gasly and Pérez get two sentences each — length tracks significance correctly

top_fixes: Cut 'Until next week' entirely — the piece ends when the last entry (Pérez) ends; the standings and Madrid preview are a summary paragraph that violates S2 and softens the close

Rewrite the 'Morning' section to open on an evaluative claim rather than 'If you only caught…' — it currently narrates the experience of watching rather than delivering a verdict; the whole section could be cut or collapsed into the red-flag section without loss

Remove 'I think it matters more than anything else in this piece' — first-person is earned here but the self-referential framing ('in this piece') breaks R3; replace with the claim stated flatly and let the emphasis do the work
